---
title: "repo"
toc: true
---

The `repo` subcommand is used to set up repositories.

## Commands

```
  repo readme
  repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]
  repo action <action-name>
  repo install repos
```

## `repo readme`

This command interacts with the user to scaffold a standardized `README.md` for a project repository.

When executed, it prompts for the following information:
- The project title.
- A brief description of what the repository does.
- The full names and email addresses of two primary contacts.

It then generates a `README.md` using the provided inputs.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The generated `README.md` follows a clean template containing sections for the title, purpose, contact details, links (e.g. data sources, publications), and further details (e.g. methods, timeline, team, data sources).

For example, the output might look like:

```markdown
# My Project Title

This repository handles data processing for the survey data.

## Contact

For more information, please contact:
- Jane Doe:
  - jane.doe@example.com
- John Smith:
  - john.smith@example.com

## Links

- [URLs to data sources (e.g. OneDrive), GitHub repositories, publications, etc.]

## Details

[Methods, timeline, team, data sources, software/tools, etc.]
```
:::

## `repo devcontainer`

This command copies a reference `.devcontainer` configuration into your current repository.

```bash
setupmjr repo devcontainer [--repo <owner>/<repo>@<branch>] [--build]
```

- `--repo`: Specifies the source repository and branch to copy the `.devcontainer` directory from (defaults to `MiguelRodo/comp@main`).
- `--build`: If provided, the command will also download the relevant GitHub Action to automatically prebuild the devcontainer, fetching good default settings from the reference actions.

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

The source archive is downloaded completely to a temporary file before extraction, so a timeout or interrupted HTTP body cannot feed a partial archive into `tar`. Repository and branch values are passed as command arguments rather than interpolated into a shell command. If `--build` is passed, the `prebuild-devcontainer.yml` workflow download is staged before replacing the destination file.

setupmjr-owned HTTP downloads use a finite request timeout and report the request URL and HTTP status on failures such as `403 Forbidden`. Failed or incomplete file downloads are discarded rather than being left at their final destination path.
:::

## `repo install repos`

While `setupmjr` has a few subcommands like `repo`, the `repos` command is actually a dependency of `setupmjr`. The `setupmjr repo install repos` command downloads and installs this external `repos` utility into `~/.local/bin`. The release archive is staged in a temporary directory and is not extracted after a failed or incomplete download.

The core operations for managing repositories (cloning, configuring workspaces, etc.) are conceptually part of `repos`, which `setupmjr` uses or exposes.

## `repo action`

This command simplifies adding pre-configured GitHub Actions to your repository.

```bash
setupmjr repo action <action-name>
```

It downloads the specified action workflow from the [MiguelRodo/actions](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/actions) repository into your `.github/workflows/` directory.

### Available Actions

The following actions can be added:

- **`prebuild-devcontainer`**: Builds and pushes a pre-built Dev Container image to GHCR whenever a SemVer tag is pushed. Read more [here](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/actions/tree/main/prebuild-devcontainer).
- **`publish-quarto-site`**: Renders and publishes a Quarto site to the `gh-pages` branch whenever the main branch is updated. Read more [here](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/actions/tree/main/publish-quarto-site).
- **`version-release`**: Bumps versions in Python or R packages, creates a versioned git tag, and publishes a GitHub Release. Read more [here](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/actions/tree/main/version-release).

::: {.callout-info collapse="true"}
## Details

When `repo action <action-name>` needs to fetch a workflow example from `MiguelRodo/actions`, the new file is staged in `.github/workflows/` and replaces the final path only after the download completes successfully.
:::
